name: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Bājūrī
summary: Shaykh al-Azhar from 1847, whose glosses on the madrasa's short texts include one on al-ʿImrīṭī's versification of al-Ājurrūmiyya.
bio: Al-Bājūrī was born in Bājūr in the Nile Delta, studied at al-Azhar and became its shaykh in 1263/1847. He wrote glosses on many of the short books the Azhar read, in law, theology, logic and grammar, and they travelled with the books, as far as Southeast Asia. In grammar his Fatḥ rabb al-bariyya explains al-ʿImrīṭī's al-Durra al-bahiyya, the poem made from al-Ājurrūmiyya. He died in Cairo in 1276/1860.

works.title: Fatḥ rabb al-bariyya ʿalā al-Durra al-bahiyya

uncertain: His death is given as 1276/1860 or 1277/1860–61.
